title: ERD Studio logical model
description: One logical model: .erd-studio/logical-models/{name}.yml or .erd-studio/logical-models/{folder}/{name}.yml. Shared by every domain that lists its name. Reference: https://github.com/liam-machine/erd-studio/blob/main/docs/semantic-domain-json-reference.md#model-files-erd-studiological-modelsfoldernameyml

$schema.description: Optional schema reference for editors outside VS Code. Ignored by ERD Studio.

name.description: Model name — its identity everywhere (domain files, relationships, positions). Must equal the file name without .yml and be unique across the whole model library.

schema.description: Target schema the model materialises in.

alias.description: Warehouse table name when it differs from `name` (dbt's `alias` config). Letters, digits and underscores; must not start with a digit. The canvas shows the alias as the model's label.

tableRole.description: The table naming's name for "modelRole", in .erd-studio/tables/ (#162). Write one of the two, as the project's naming says.

relationships.description: Relationships that leave this model, defined once for the whole project: every domain that holds both this model and toModel draws the edge. They live with the model holding the foreign key (the "many" side), so a new fact never means editing its dimensions: ERD Studio stores a one-to-many the other way round, as many-to-one on the other model. The same fields as a domain file's relationship, without fromModel (it is this model).

modelRole.description: The model's role in the warehouse architecture.

rationale.description: The table's built-in text fields (context fields), under camelCase keys (openQuestions, not open_questions). Every field is optional; omit the whole object when it would be empty. Team fields go in meta. The canvas shows an "R" badge on models that have one.

purpose.description: Purpose: who uses this table and the question it answers.

decisions.description: Decisions: a choice a later editor might undo, and why.

openQuestions.description: Open questions: what is still undecided. Assistants ask about these and never guess.

design.description: Retired (Design): still read and shown. Move its text to decisions, or to purpose.

grainChoice.description: Retired (Grain choice): still read and shown. Move its text to decisions.

roleChoice.description: Retired (Role choice): still read and shown. Move its text to decisions.

scdStrategy.description: History: how this dimension keeps history — which columns track changes and which overwrite.

measures.description: Measures: how the measures add up — which sum across every dimension and which do not.

sourceOfTruth.description: Source of truth: the system this data is mastered in.

freshness.description: Freshness: how fresh it must be, and how often it loads.

knownIssues.description: Known issues: data problems a consumer should know before trusting a number.

retention.description: Retention: how long rows are kept, and why.

dataType.description: SQL data type, e.g. STRING, INTEGER, BOOLEAN, DATE, DECIMAL(18,2), TIMESTAMP_NTZ, VARCHAR.

isPrimaryKey.description: Primary key. Only include when true.

isForeignKey.description: Foreign key intent. Only include when true; the relationship itself lives in the domain file.

isNaturalKey.description: Business identifier (email, SKU, customer_code). Only include when true.

scdType.description: Dimension columns: how the attribute handles change.

additiveType.description: Fact measures: how the measure aggregates across dimensions.

meta.description: Your team's own fields — owner, source system, lineage, anything .erd-studio/fields.yml lists or your team records — in the shape of dbt's `meta:`. Free-form: values may be text, numbers, true/false, lists or nested maps. The canvas shows them in the Detail panel's fields and edits top-level text values; ERD Studio never compares them with dbt.

toModel.description: Referenced model (PK side). A relationship whose toModel has no model file is not drawn.

toTable.description: The table naming's name for "toModel", in .erd-studio/tables/ (#162).

cardinality.description: Relationship cardinality, read from fromModel to toModel. In a model file, write many-to-one, one-to-one or many-to-many: one-to-many is deprecated here.
enumDescriptions: Many rows of this model point at one row of toModel. This model holds the foreign key.
One row of this model points at one row of toModel. This model holds the foreign key.

Deprecated in model files: still read, but it is the same relationship as a many-to-one stored on toModel. ERD Studio writes it that way round, in toModel's file, and Move Relationships to Model Library moves it there.

role.description: Optional label for what this link means, e.g. "order date" and "ship date" for two columns pointing at the same date dimension. A label only; it is not part of the relationship's identity.

compositeKey.description: Entries of this file that share this value form one composite foreign key: one relationship over several column pairs, drawn as one line. Each entry is one column pair; all must point at the same toModel with the same cardinality (many-to-one or one-to-one). ERD Studio 1.6.7 and earlier read the entries as separate relationships and drop this key when they save the file.
